articles.title: （深圳APEC）专访郑永年：西方唱衰中国经济毫无道理，商界知道动力在哪

articles.title: Embrace Your Obsessions: Susan Orlean on the Antidote to the Meaninglessness of Life
articles.highlight: 每一部伟大的书，无论题材、体裁或风格，都只关乎一件事：什么赋予我们渺小短暂的生命以意义。
articles.summary: 文章围绕苏珊·奥尔琳的写作与痴迷展开，指出伟大的书最终都在追问什么赋予短暂生命以意义，而答案在于我们如何关注生活。它提醒读者，对微小而独特之物的专注，是把爱转化为意义的支点，因此值得一读。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键启发是：意义未必来自宏大目标，而来自对具体、微小事物的持续关注；痴迷若被安放为专注，就能削弱恐惧与痛苦。
articles.sourceExcerpt: Every great book, whatever its subject or genre or style, is about one thing only: the eternal question of what gives meaning to our tiny, transient lives. And every answer given, however faintly whispered, points to one thing only: the quality of attention we pay to those lives. If attention is the lever of love, the particular — the sacred specificity of something small and singular, something easy to overlook — is its fulcrum.

en.highlight: Every great book, whatever its subject or genre or style, is about one thing only: what gives meaning to our tiny, transient lives.
en.summary: Drawing on Susan Orlean’s writing and sense of obsession, the piece argues that great books ultimately ask what gives meaning to our brief lives, and that the answer lies in the quality of attention we give them. It is worth reading as a reminder that focused attention to small, singular things can turn love into meaning.
en.failureAnalysis: The key takeaway is that meaning often comes not from grand goals but from sustained attention to the specific and the small; obsession, when channeled as focus, can blunt fear and pain.
